item.title: Brand-New Division Game is Already Being Review Bombed
item.description:
The Division Resurgence is already being hit with a flood of negative Steam reviews just days after Ubisoft brought the free-to-play spin-off to Valve's PC storefront. As a new story in the post-pandemic universe of The Division , The Division Resurgence adapts the series' familiar looter-shooter formula around a free-to-play structure previously limited to mobile devices.

The Division 2 Reveals 10 Year Anniversary Plans and Teases Next Big DLC

Massive Entertainment reveals the 2026 roadmap for The Division 2 which includes a 10 year anniversary celebration, Survivors, and new DLC.

By Derek Nichols

The Division Resurgence Launches to Brutal Steam Reviews

Following The Division Resurgence 's August 5 release on Steam, the game has been met with a wave of negative reviews. Players have repeatedly targeted the title's loot boxes, microtransactions, level-gated progression, and limits on how quickly rewards can be earned as the game's biggest issues. One Steam reviewer complained about "heavy menu clutter, loot boxes, and monetization shortcuts," while another described the gameplay loop as being built around grinding levels repeatedly just to unlock basic story objectives. Overall, timed progression gates are among the most common complaints, as some of the game's most valuable rewards become harder to obtain once players exhaust their limited daily opportunities. The "Most Helpful" review at time of publication says, "Calling it slop disrespects actual slop," with 126 users flagging the post as "helpful." As of this writing, The Division Resurgence holds a "Mixed" Steam rating, with only 45% of roughly 1,620 user reviews being positive.

Tom Clancy's The Division Resurgence

item.title: 7 R-Rated Open-World RPGs That Can Be Called Masterpieces
item.description:
"R-rated" might not be the official ESRB term, but as a cultural shorthand, it serves as the ultimate gatekeeper to a world of adult storytelling, visceral violence, weighty themes, and maybe even a bit of skin. While not plentiful, R-rated open-world RPGs are among the genre's most beloved representatives, and they take many forms. Some lean into horror, others explore tragedy, while a few embrace surreal insanity.

Even though I don't believe a game needs to be R/M-rated to tell a mature story, loosening restrictions simply allows developers to explore ideas more brazenly without needing to wear kid gloves. Just because a title pulls none of its punches doesn't mean it is great, but these open-world RPGs are simply all-time masterpieces.

The best thing about focusing on "R-rated" games is that we aren't married to ESRB. We can include PC-only releases with no rating!

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Is The Definitive Mature Open-World RPG Masterpiece

CD Projekt Red Has No Issue Going Full Dark Fantasy

Let's get the most obvious one out of the way. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt will be everyone's first vision when they imagine an "R-rated open-world RPG." Quests like Bloody Baron, Tower of Mice, La Cage au Fou, and the entirety of "Hearts of Stone" were seemingly created to haunt our dreams, break our spirits, and hurt our souls, and they more than succeeded. A pure dark low fantasy world, Geralt's adventures are often defined by gray areas, sadness, and futility.

The Definitive Open-World Games Tier List For 2026

Let's appreciate some of the finest open-world games since 2015 by organizing them into tiers.

3
By Anastasia Maillot

The Witcher 3 's maturity goes well beyond the occasionally gory moment or Geralt bathing; the writing defines itself through nuance and human exploration, rarely providing easy or satisfying answers. Nearly every character carries scars that shape or blind them, chasing their version of "good" by often relying on the unthinkable.

Cyberpunk 2077 qualifies as a masterpiece, too, but I didn't want to double-down on CD Projekt Red.

Kenshi Lets Us Become The Darkness

Surviving In Hell With Other Humans

From a narrative juggernaut to an emergent gameplay cult masterpiece, Kenshi delivers an entirely different sort of experience than nearly every open-world RPG, and you get to write your journey. Regardless of what path you take, a street paved with brutality awaits, requiring and reinforcing acts that demonstrate humanity at its most desperate and ruthless. As you walk and adapt, you will become both the victim and perpetrator.

Kenshi doesn't tell a story, instead simply dropping players into a world that allows for cannibalism, systemic slavery, cartels, dismemberment, and skin stealers. Survive, thrive, or succumb; whatever may happen, the world eventually consumes you.

Elden Ring Drops You In A Cosmic Horror Playground

Fear Gods, Abominations, And Dung Eaters

The second "obvious" R-rated open-world RPG, Elden Ring expanded the FromSoftware formula into a sandbox, retaining the impeccable boss design, cryptic lore, and penchant for both overt and hidden nightmares. The first major legacy dungeon boss, Godrick the Grafted, stitched dozens of human limbs onto his body; later on, players fight Rykard, who fed himself to an ancient serpent to become a pure Lovecraftian monster.

Elden Ring excels in body horror, but its darkest points don't rely on that. Dung Eater's storyline would get a 3-part special on The Last Podcast on the Left , while the Omen Curse lore turns Morgott and Moh into two incredibly sympathetic characters. That's really just the tip of this horrifying iceberg, and once you dive beneath the surface, all you find is Godwyn's rotting corpse that refuses to die.

Pathologic 2 Forces You To Live With Your Choices

A True Open-World Horror RPG

You know what, let's stick with the horror vibes for a bit longer, and Pathologic 2 isn't just adjacent to that genre. A rare open-world horror RPG, Ice-Pick Lodge crafts an intensely oppressive environment that forces players to make stressful decisions that nearly always end with consequences.

You portray a surgeon who returns to his plague-infested hometown as it descends into violence amidst paranoia, psychological exhaustion, and moral decay. Signaling out every "dark" element would involve writing a full synopsis, but Pathologic 2 elevates its organ harvesting, child sacrifice, and autopsies through player choice, harsh failure, and permanent reminders of your mistakes.

The 20 Best Open-World Horror Games

Open-world games are often thought of in terms of RPGs, but these horror games make excellent use of the open-world format.

3
By Amy Cowley

Gothic Was The Original R-Rated Open-World RPG Masterpiece

And It Still Is Pretty Good

If someone didn't play Gothic back in the day, its brilliance can be hard to appreciate because of the general jankiness that permeates the gameplay... however, make no mistake about it: this Eurojank masterpiece was wildly ambitious and impressive in 2001, and its most important ideas stand the test of time. When you arrive in the penal colony of Khorinis, the game treats you like dirt, creating an open world where you must earn respect, safety, and survival through blood, grit, and political bribery.

Once you get over the steep learning curve, Gothic begins to shine as an immersive RPG (or even sim, to be honest) set in a society ruled by hierarchy, rackets, cults, and exploitation. While unrefined in places, the storytelling generally rocks and combines really well with the all-time great progression system.

Kingdom Come Deliverance 2 Is An R-Rated History Lesson

Reality Is Darker Than Fantasy

Gothic 's influence can be seen in plenty of modern RPGs, and Kingdom Come Deliverance and its sequel might be the most successful evolutions. While historical in nature, Warhorse's games adopt Gothic 's progression and tone, rejecting high-fantasy magic in favor of immersion and authenticity.

You might be surprised to learn that 15th-century Europe wasn't the most pleasant place to live in, especially if you are a lowly blacksmith dragged into a war between kingdoms. KCD2 doesn't hide the atrocities that were commonplace during this era, and the punishing combat and systems heighten that sense of danger.

Dread Delusion Is A Masterclass In Strangeness

An Open-World RPG Doesn't Need Photorealistic Graphics To Be Uncomfortable

Let's end things with a weird one! Dread Delusion blends PS1 visuals with Morrowind and then turns the "surreal horror" dial up to 10. Due to a curse, the Endless Realm rejects death, forcing citizens to live on as their bodies decompose. Towns become sentient mass graves filled with echoes of people mourning the remnants of their lives, while existing at the mercy of a ruling faction that demands obedience.

Walking through Dread Delusion 's world feels like wandering through a fever dream. I recognize everything, but nothing seems quite right, and things only get worse the longer the dream lasts. I wouldn't necessarily recommend this game to everyone, but if you want a true psychopathic horror RPG, Dread Delusion might be the best.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 CEO Releases Official Statement on Christmas Discounts
item.description:
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick recently spoke about possible Christmas discounts, among other things, on Grand Theft Auto 6 during a televised interview. It's worth noting that, aside from this kernel of insight into possible holiday plans for GTA 6 , Zelnick stuck to most talking points that fans are certainly already aware of.

He reiterated that GTA 6 pre-orders were exceptional, that he believes Rockstar will exceed expectations, that the $100 edition has received the most pre-orders so far, and that the GTA 6: Extended Look on Netflix will be worth watching. Indeed, these have been his main talking points over the past few days, and for those looking to pick the game up day one on November 19, this information only reinforces that. Anyone who may want to wait for a sale, however, may unsurprisingly be waiting for a while.

Rockstar Releases New Official GTA 6 In-Game Screenshot

Rockstar Games releases a new official Grand Theft Auto 6 screenshot for fans to analyze and debate.

3
By Dalton Cooper

GTA Won't Receive Discounts Directly From Rockstar/Take-Two

Zelnick discussed GTA 6 during a televised interview appearance on CNBC, where a host asked about holiday discount plans or if there would be any. Zelnick did not rule out the possibility entirely, but he made it very clear that the discount would not be coming from Rockstar or Take-Two itself. He explained that what retailers do is out of his control, noting that any discount given would come out of their margin of profit on GTA 6 , but that the two companies intend to preserve the price of GTA 6 for a long time. Specifically, he said,

"We obviously established our pricing, and storefronts can do what they wish. We don't have any ability to control, so if they reduce the price, they are reducing their margin on the sale. There are certain situations where certain retailers will price down to drive demand for other things they sell, so I can't tell what will happen. What I can tell you is that we preserved our pricing on Grand Theft Auto 5 for a long time, much longer than the standard release of an entertainment product."

Zelnick's remarks bring to mind comments on Nintendo and why it never discounts games. In short, Nintendo believes its games are "the best" and a result of "Kyoto craftmanship," a local belief that the company overdelivers the initial asking price and therefore it becomes a "fair price" always. It's a belief in the quality of the game, regardless of if it's 5 years old or 10 years old, although discounts can rarely happen. Given that Zelnick believes Rockstar overdelivers on GTA 6 , it'll be interesting to see if its pricing is preserved for as long as GTA 5.

After all, there's much more than the initial release of Grand Theft Auto 6 to consider. Details are scarce and essentially non-existent, but Take-Two wanting to launch a Grand Theft Auto 6 Online sometime after the core game should surprise no one. Depending on how it's packaged, that could go a long way in supporting the price preservation and demand of the game as well.

Grand Theft Auto 6 CEO Releases Official Statement on Christmas Discounts
Take-Two Releases New Official Statement on GTA 6 Online
Next GTA 6 Update is Locked Behind a $8.99 Paywall
Take-Two Reveals Why GTA 6 Extended Look Is On Netflix

Ultimately, it all remains to be seen. What cannot be ignored here, when discussing GTA 6 's price and release date, is the ongoing economic strain. Many households are struggling with necessities, not just entertainment products, so it remains to be seen how that impacts Grand Theft Auto 6 , if at all. That said, there's a very good chance that, for many households, it is the only and only gift planned for the holiday season—fingers crossed that Rockstar craftsmanship rings true at release and this holiday season.
